title: Hard to misuse
description:
`Rectangle r{ 10, 20 };` Which is the width? A reader has to go and look, and a caller can swap them without any complaint from the compiler.

Make the mistake impossible. Write two tiny wrapper types and a rectangle that insists on them:

- `struct Width` and `struct Height`, each with one `double value` member and an **explicit** constructor from `double`;
- `class Rectangle` with the constructor `Rectangle(Width width, Height height)` and `double area() const`.

`Rectangle{ Width{ 10 }, Height{ 20 } }` compiles. `Rectangle{ 10, 20 }` and `Rectangle{ Height{ 20 }, Width{ 10 } }` must not; the tests check all three at compile time.
